RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Reference Number: POC-DA651E8611-76145
Member: Cameron Jennings, Member ID W378650128
Date of Notice: 2026-08-22
Requested Service/CPT: Total shoulder replacement, CPT 23472
Treating Surgeon: Okafor, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Appeals Review Committee:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for total shoulder arthroplasty (CPT 23472), as stated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-22. The stated reason for denial was that "the requested procedure does not meet the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria" for medical necessity. I am submitting this appeal within the 180-day window identified in that notice (due by 2027-02-18).

The denial notice did not quote or attach the specific medical-necessity criteria applied to my case. Based on my own research, the document that appears to govern prior authorization review of shoulder arthroplasty for this plan is the Carelon Medical Benefits Management Clinical Appropriateness Guideline titled "Musculoskeletal Appropriate Use Criteria: Joint Surgery," Shoulder Arthroplasty section (Doc ID MSK02-1125.1, effective 11/15/2025). If a different or plan-specific medical policy was actually used to review my request, I ask that the plan identify that document by title, number, and effective date, and provide me a full copy, since it was not included with the denial notice. Everything below that I place in quotation marks is text I was able to independently verify from the above Carelon guideline; everything else is my own description of my clinical record and is not a quotation of the plan's policy.

**1. The guideline's description of when total (anatomic) shoulder arthroplasty is used**

The guideline states: "Shoulder arthroplasty includes several procedures to replace components of the shoulder joint, in part or in total, with the goal of improving function and reducing pain. Prosthetic replacement of the humeral head and the glenoid (total arthroplasty) is most commonly performed for joint damage due to osteoarthritis. Total shoulder arthroplasty requires an intact medial glenoid to support the glenoid prosthesis."

My CT imaging dated 2026-07-21 confirms an intact rotator cuff, which is consistent with anatomic total shoulder arthroplasty (rather than reverse arthroplasty, which is used when the cuff is deficient). This supports that CPT 23472 — not a different arthroplasty procedure — is the clinically appropriate request in my case.

**2. The specific clinical indication for total shoulder arthroplasty due to advanced joint disease**

The guideline states: "Total shoulder arthroplasty is considered medically necessary for ANY of the following indications: Proximal humerus fracture confirmed by imaging not amenable to internal fixation (e.g., severe comminution, poor bone quality, multipart, displaced) Malignancy involving the glenohumeral joint or surrounding soft tissue Advanced joint disease of the shoulder due to osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, avascular necrosis (osteonecrosis), or post-traumatic arthritis when ALL the following requirements are met: Limited range of motion or crepitus of the glenohumeral joint on physical examination · Pain and loss of function of at least 6 months' duration that interferes with daily activities (unless radiographs show Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4) *Radiographic evidence of destructive degenerative joint disease as evidenced by marked joint space narrowing AND ONE or more of the following:"

(Note: I was not able to independently retrieve the full text of the remaining radiographic sub-bullets that follow "AND ONE or more of the following," and I am not quoting or guessing at that language. I ask the plan to apply my imaging findings, described below, against that specific sub-list and to send me the complete text of that section.)

My clinical record documents each of the elements above that I was able to verify:

- **Pain and loss of function well beyond 6 months:** I have had 24 months of progressive shoulder pain, unrelieved by rest, with resulting inability to reach overhead, dress without help, or sleep on the affected side.
- **Limited range of motion and crepitus on physical examination:** My exam documents glenohumeral crepitus, active forward elevation limited to 90 degrees, and external rotation limited to 10 degrees, with intact cuff strength.
- **Radiographic evidence of destructive degenerative joint disease with marked joint space narrowing:** Shoulder radiographs (true AP and axillary) dated 2026-07-21 show complete loss of glenohumeral joint space, osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis, and a flattened glenoid.

The guideline also states, regarding imaging documentation generally: "Imaging reports should be thorough and describe the presence or absence of subchondral cysts, subchondral sclerosis, periarticular osteophytes, joint subluxation, avascular necrosis, or bone on bone articulations. The degree of joint space narrowing should also be noted." My 2026-07-21 imaging report documents exactly these elements — subchondral sclerosis, periarticular osteophytes, and complete (bone-on-bone) joint space loss — which I believe satisfies the guideline's own description of adequate radiographic documentation for this indication.

**3. The guideline's general framework for confirming medical necessity**

The guideline's General Clinical Guideline section states that clinical appropriateness depends on the clinician having "confirm[ed] the diagnosis or establish[ed] its pretest likelihood based on a complete evaluation of the patient. This includes a history and physical examination and, where applicable, a review of relevant laboratory studies, diagnostic testing, and response to prior therapeutic intervention," that "the anticipated benefit of the recommended intervention is likely to outweigh any potential harms," and that "there exists a reasonable likelihood that the intervention will change management and/or lead to an improved outcome for the patient."

My record documents exactly this kind of complete evaluation and trial of therapy prior to the arthroplasty request:

- **Physical therapy:** 8 weeks of supervised physical therapy (18 visits, 2026-06-06 through 2026-08-01) focused on range-of-motion and periscapular strengthening, per the physical therapy discharge note, without resolution of my symptoms.
- **Medication trial:** NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief.
- **Injection trial:** Corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-31, which gave only 3 weeks of partial relief before symptoms returned.
- **Diagnostic evaluation:** Radiographs and CT dated 2026-07-21 confirming end-stage glenohumeral joint disease with an intact rotator cuff.

Given the severity and chronicity of my joint destruction (complete loss of joint space, osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis, flattened glenoid) and my documented failure to improve with an extensive, multi-modality conservative treatment trial, I believe there is a reasonable likelihood that total shoulder arthroplasty will improve my function and relieve my pain, consistent with the general framework quoted above.

**4. Absence of disqualifying factors**

I do not have an active shoulder infection, I have no untreated substance use, my BMI is 29, and I am a non-smoker. I note that the guideline separately identifies tobacco cessation "for at least 6 weeks prior to surgery" as "strongly recommended"; as a non-smoker, this is not a barrier in my case. I was not able to independently retrieve the specific text of the guideline's "Contraindications" section for shoulder arthroplasty, so I am not quoting it, but based on the information available to me, none of the factors typically identified as contraindications (e.g., active infection) are present in my case.

**Requested action**

Based on the above, I ask that Wellpoint:

1. Reverse the denial and approve prior authorization for CPT 23472 (total shoulder arthroplasty) as requested by Dr. Okafor;
2. If the denial is not fully reversed on this written appeal, arrange a peer-to-peer conversation between Dr. Okafor and the reviewing physician before final determination; and
3. Provide me, in writing, the complete text of the specific medical policy or clinical guideline (including the full radiographic sub-criteria referenced above) that was actually applied to my case, if it differs from the Carelon "Joint Surgery" guideline cited in this letter.

Enclosed with this appeal are copies of:

- The physical therapy discharge note (2026-06-06 to 2026-08-01, 18 visits)
- Medication and injection history (NSAID trial; corticosteroid injection 2026-05-31)
- Shoulder radiograph and CT reports dated 2026-07-21
- Physical examination notes documenting range-of-motion and crepitus findings
- Surgeon's (Dr. Okafor) letter of medical necessity [attach if available]

Please send written acknowledgment of receipt of this appeal and notify me and Dr. Okafor's office of the outcome and of any further documentation needed, using the contact information below.

Sincerely,
